en.headline: Medical Council rejects target time frames for handling complaints
en.dek: The watchdog told Legco a statutory requirement for milestones is unnecessary and can be handled administratively, as it responded to a government reform bill.
body: Hong Kong’s Medical Council has rejected a government proposal to require public target time frames for specific steps in its complaints procedure, saying the measure is unnecessary and can be managed administratively.

In a written submission to the Legislative Council bills committee dated Tuesday and uploaded the following day, council chairwoman Professor Grace Tang Wai-king said a dedicated working group had studied the Medical Registration (Amendment) Bill. The government first outlined the reforms in late June, aiming to speed up complaint handling and increase accountability.

Among other proposed changes, the bill would alter disciplinary sentencing options, internal supervision and the proportion of lay members. The council stated that setting milestones for document submissions and inquiries did not need to be stipulated in law, noting that government departments and other statutory bodies already handle similar matters administratively.

zh.headline: 醫委會反對投訴處理設法定時限
zh.dek: 醫委會書面回應立法會指無需在法例訂明各步驟目標時限，可按現行行政方式處理，並就政府改革草案提出意見。
body: 香港醫務委員會反對政府建議在法例中規定投訴處理各步驟的公開目標時限，認為並無必要，可按行政方式處理。
醫委會主席鄧惠琼教授在周二提交立法會法案委員會的書面意見中表示，已成立專責工作小組研究《醫生註冊（修訂）條例草案》細節。政府早前於6月底提出改革，旨在加快處理投訴及加強問責。
草案亦涉及紀律處分方式、內部監督及增加業外委員比例等改動。醫委會指訂明文件提交及研訊里程碑無需寫入法例，政府部門及其他法定機構已以行政方式處理同類事宜。
